finding.R1: A nested pytest_collection_finish wrapper marked tryfirst and wrapper=True can be outer to the owned wrapper; its post-yield registration of pytest_runtestloop happened after collection-finish validation and could suppress the entire test loop.
finding.R2: A normal executor registered after an item call boundary, including a yield-fixture teardown or setup-skip logreport, could replace pytest_runtest_protocol for a later item. A final-item teardown could also register after the last boundary and leave a zero native exit looking complete.
finding.control: The bridge now validates before pytest_runtestloop yield, before every pytest_runtest_protocol yield, retains the pytest_runtest_call check, and validates the retained plugin manager after pytest.main returns before terminal_complete is set. Boundary checks are unconditional. Refusal returns 4 only when the observed native exit is zero; a genuine observed nonzero remains the bridge exit and report bridge_exit_code.
finding.scope: Ordinary persistent unowned pytest execution hooks in the basic_serial scoped bridge. This is not a hostile-code sandbox and does not claim to prevent arbitrary same-user project side effects before refusal.
